retrieval: Primary full text opened with web tool; methods and normal-tissue sections read.
findings: Normal panel: 17 adult samples from breast, colon, kidney, lung and uterus, plus 10 fetal bowel/lung/kidney samples.
Study explicitly lacks tissue-of-origin normal matches for several cancers; matched analyses concern breast, colon and lung.
Samples were drawn from Stanford sources; distinct specimen labels alone do not establish distinct patients across studies.
Peak discovery used pooled cancer libraries; the peak matrix is not an unbiased census of expression in normal tissues.
Values were depth-scaled and square-root compressed; they are not raw counts or absolute RNA abundance.
consequence: The retrieved per-library matrix removes a local availability barrier, but cannot by itself supply broad normal-organ coverage or establish cross-study patient independence. No biological comparison has been executed.
next_evidence: Check sample linkage and appropriate within-study contrasts before claiming independent validation; retain organ-limited and assay-limited scope.
